title: Chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetallic state through enhanced correlation in CeGaGe
authors: Arushi, Kevin Allen, Yuan Fang, Kuan-Sen Lin, Mounica Mahankali, Hari Bhandari, Karthik Rao, Alberto Ruiz Biestro, Christopher Lane, Jian-Xin Zhu, Sanu Mishra, Geoffroy Hautier, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan
abstract: Strongly correlated chiral materials have been proposed to host a chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetal (cWKSM) state, in which Kondo hybridization pins chirality-induced Kramers-Weyl point crossings, together with additional symmetry-enforced band crossings, near the Fermi level. Realizing this state requires a material that combines crystal chirality, non-symmorphic symmetry, and Kondo correlations, and currently there are no known materials that combine all these requirements. Here we report evidence for a cWKSM state in CeGaGe, a member of the RXY (R = rare earth; X = Al, Si; Y = Ga, Ge) family. Magnetization measurements confirm long-range antiferromagnetic order below T$_N$ = 4.7 K with a complex, canted magnetic structure. Unique to CeGaGe among the known RXY systems is a structural transition from an achiral tetragonal I4$_{1}$md structure (at high temperatures) to the chiral tetragonal P4$_{3}$ structure (at low temperatures). The structural transition in CeGaGe allows us to highlight the role of chirality in stabilizing the Kramers cWKSM state. Hall resistivity measurements with $H || c$ reveal an anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) that is constant below the Kondo temperature $T_K \approx 7$ K and drops sharply above it. This crossover tracks the onset of Kondo coherence rather than the magnetic ordering, which occurs at T$_N$ = 4.7 K. Together with first-principles calculations for the $P4_3$ structure, this identifies the AHC as an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven contribution generated by Kondo hybridization, rather than a consequence of extrinsic scattering or dynamic scalar spin chirality. These results establish CeGaGe as a rare experimental platform in which crystal chirality, strong electronic correlations, and non-trivial band topology coexist, providing the first material realization of a Kondo-driven cWKSM state.
summary: This work reports evidence for a chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetallic state in CeGaGe, a material that uniquely combines crystal chirality, non-symmorphic symmetry, and strong electronic correlations. By analyzing anomalous Hall conductivity and structural transitions, the authors demonstrate that the AHC is intrinsically linked to Kondo hybridization in the low-temperature phase. This establishes CeGaGe as a key experimental platform for studying Kondo-driven topological semimetallics.
main_problem: To establish the first experimental realization of a chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetal (cWKSM) state, which requires the confluence of crystal chirality, non-symmorphic symmetry, and Kondo correlations.
main_result: The material CeGaGe exhibits evidence for a cWKSM state in its low-temperature phase, confirmed by anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) behavior tracking Kondo coherence. This establishes CeGaGe as a rare platform realizing this complex correlated topological state.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (magnetization, Hall resistivity, specific heat) with first-principles DFT calculations and theoretical toy models to analyze the electronic structure and topological properties.
model_or_system: The physical system is CeGaGe, which undergoes a structural transition to a chiral, non-centrosymmetric $P4_3$ phase. The theoretical analysis employs a Periodic Anderson Lattice Model and a toy model to incorporate Kondo hybridization effects into the band structure.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall Conductivity (AHC), Kondo temperature ($T_K$), magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N$), and the Berry curvature ($\Omega_{ij}(\mathbf{k})$).
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K \approx 7-8 	ext{ K}$), Néel temperature ($T_N = 4.7 	ext{ K}$), and the structural transition temperature ($T_{struct} = 230 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The AHC is assumed to be an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven contribution from Kondo hybridization, and theoretical calculations rely on approximations like the saddle-point method.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural transition ($I4_1md 	o P4_3$), magnetic ordering, Kondo correlations via specific heat, and electronic band structures showing Berry curvature maps at different $k_z$ values.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the necessary ingredients (chirality, symmetry, correlations), presenting experimental evidence (structural/magnetic transitions, AHC measurements), and finally using theoretical models (toy models, Berry curvature calculations) to confirm the cWKSM state in the low-temperature phase.
why_interesting: The interplay between structural phase transitions, strong electronic correlations (Kondo effect), and topological band structures (Weyl points) is a frontier area in condensed matter physics, highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena.
